newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Brother-in-law says Netanyahu a traitor.
newsitem.headline: Brother-in-law says Netanyahu a traitor.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's family woes took a political turn on Sunday when his right-wing brother-in-law quit the ruling Likud party, accusing Israel's leader of betraying the cause.
"I feel that Bibi personally and the Likud as a party betrayed the electorate...and that is why I have decided to leave the Likud," Hagi Ben-Artzi, brother of first lady Sara Netanyahu, told Reuters.

It was the latest in a series of family spats to plague the Israeli leader, 47, since he came to power in June portraying himself as a public husband and father. Other tiffs have pitted wife Sara against nannies and an ex-husband.

A religious Jew, Ben-Artzi accused Netanyahu of heading into a peace deal with the Palestinians that would endanger the lives of the 400 Jews who live and study in the West Bank town of Hebron surrounded by 100,000 Arabs.

Ben-Artzi, a father of three who has lived in the West Bank for at least 17 years, said he would move to Hebron himself in protest later on Sunday. He said his heart was in the holy city, the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham.

"Sometimes families are torn because different members of the family have different commitments...That's a pity but I say again that my basic commitment is to the Jewish and Zionist values in which I believe," Ben-Artzi said.
Netanyahu's adviser David Bar-Illan declined comment on the prime minister's problems with his brother-in-law.

Israel and the Palestinians have been trying to hammer out an accord on the long-promised Israeli troop pullback from Hebron, the last of seven West Bank cities due to be handed over to Palestinian rule under a 1995 peace deal.
Netanyahu opposed the self-rule deal signed by the Labour party government he ousted. But he vowed to stick to the deal and Israel's other international commitments.

Ben-Artzi said he could not envisage Israel pressing ahead with the Hebron peace deal after gun battles and clashes last month claimed the lives of 15 Israeli soldiers. Sixty Palestinians were also killed.
He said Netanyahu was now following the path of Labour party prime ministers Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres.
"What I see now is he is just going in their way without any real substantial change and that's why I am so disappointed," said Ben-Artzi, who campaigned for Netanyahu's election.
He said he didn't know how his sister felt.

Sara Netanyahu, 37, was propelled into the media spotlight soon after her husband took office when a nanny she sacked over burnt soup accused the first lady of being a harsh taskmaster with a sharp temper.
Earlier this month Sara was back in the tabloids when her first husband threatened to publish a book about their six-year marriage. He later backed down.

Netanyahu also came under fire on Sunday from the widow of a soldier killed in the September violence. The battles erupted after Netanyahu punched a second opening in an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem's walled Old City.

"He opened the tunnel without asking anyone...not my husband, not the army, not his friends, no one. And then the events transpired," Sharha Mari, widow of Lieutenant-Colonel Nabi Mari, told Israel Radio.
"Look how many casualties were caused. But I paid a dear price. I paid with my husband," she said.
